newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home sales jump in Q3 from year ago -- report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home sales jump in Q3 from year ago -- report.

text.p: California existing home sales jumped 15.5 percent during the third quarter compared with a year ago, according to a report issued Thursday.
California Association of Realtors said home sales increased during the third quarter from a year ago in 198 of more than 300 selected California cities and areas.

Statewide, 515,170 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow in the third quarter on a seasonally adjusted, annualized basis, down 0.4 percent from an annualized rate of 517,320 sales in the second quarter of 1996.
Third-quarter sales jumped 15.5 percent from the third-quarter 1995 pace, when 445,880 homes were sold on an annualized basis.

"California home sales essentially held steady during the third quarter, compared with the previous three-month period, while jumping sharply from a year ago," said Rick Snyder, president of the association.

Statewide, the median sales price of an existing, single-family home was $179,580 in the third quarter, virtually unchanged from $180,070 in the second quarter and $180,120 in the third quarter of 1995.

Sales of existing condominiums declined 6.3 percent during the third quarter from the previous three-month period on a non-seasonally adjusted basis. Condo sales, however, soared 22.3 percent from the third quarter of 1995.

The statewide median price of an existing condominium was $134,850 during the third quarter, down 3.4 percent from $139,620 in the second quarter and down 1.6 percent from $137,040 in the third quarter of 1995, the report found.
